the abnormal spontaneous activity in the demyelinating nerve and the role of Ca2+ in this abnormality.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
demyelination leads to a change in the electrical properties of the nerve, and this is due, in part, to the formation of Ca2+ channels in the denuded axon membrane.
Ca2+ channels are the key factors in the generation of abnormal spontaneous activity of demyelyinated nerves.
Ca2+ channels are important factors in the generation and maintenance of ectopic discharges in demyelinated nerves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ectopic firings of demyelinating nerve are due to the Ca2+ influx through the newly formed Ca2+-channels on the axolemma.
the abnormal spontaneous afferents originating from demyelinated regions are due to the abnormal Ca2+ channel activity.
the ectopic discharges of the injured nerve are mediated by the abnormal Ca2+ channels, which are formed on the naked axon membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the abnormal spontaneous afferents originating from the demyleinated nerve may be involved in the pathogenesis of pain in patients with neuropathic pain.
the ectopic discharges of the demyelinating nerve are Ca2+ channel dependent.
the ectopic firings are not only dependent on Ca2+ influx, but also on the Ca2+ concentration.
